Documentation → FortiWeb: Policies & Protection → Line Profiles

Line profiles

Declare, per classification line, which network segments it receives, which certificate class and which Web Protection Profile template a new server policy on that line starts from.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereGlobal ADOM → Administrator → Line Profiles (URL /line-profiles/)

What is it?#

A line profile states what one classification line (for example production) receives:

  • the network segments a new policy on that line may be placed in,
  • the certificate class its certificate is issued under,
  • the Web Protection Profile template it starts from,
  • optionally an IPAM pool to take addresses from.

The New Server Policy from a line wizard reads these declarations. A line without a profile still works, but SATOM then infers its segments by matching each segment's line field to the line name, and the page labels that answer as a guess.

What does it do?#

  • Shows one card per value of the Lines catalog (from Classification), with a badge: declared (a profile exists) or inferred — no profile.
  • Lists the line's Resolved segments and every problem found, each with a code. Problems that would stop policy creation are red, and the card shows blocks policy creation.
  • Lets you create, update or delete the profile of each line.

Problem codes#

Code Meaning Blocks policy creation
missing_segment The profile names a segment that no longer exists Yes
no_segments No network segment is assigned to the line Yes
duplicate_segment Two segments share a name, so the network is ambiguous Yes
wpp_gone The named WPP template no longer exists Yes
wpp_not_approved The WPP template is not approved Yes
wpp_wrong_product The WPP template belongs to another product Yes
no_cert_class No certificate class is declared No (the wizard asks)
no_wpp No WPP template is named No
segment_no_cidr A segment has no CIDR, so no address can be allocated from it No

Approval of the WPP template is checked when a policy is built, not when the profile is saved. A template rejected later blocks the line from then on.

Requirements#

  • At least one value in the Lines catalog (Classification). With an empty catalog the page says The Lines catalog is empty. Add lines in Classification first — a profile can only answer for a line that exists.
  • Network segments defined under Network Segments (Segments).
  • Optionally, an approved FortiWeb web-protection-profile template in the Template Library.

Permissions#

users.manage is required to view, save and delete (Administrator). Without it the Administrator menu group is hidden and /line-profiles/ answers 403 Forbidden. From the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator consoles the URL redirects to that console's home page.

❗Important — Profiles are FortiWeb profiles

The menu entry is in the Global ADOM, but the page always runs in the FortiWeb ADOM: opening it from Global switches that browser tab to FortiWeb. Profiles are therefore stored as FortiWeb profiles, which is what the line wizard reads, and the template list offers the FortiWeb Web Protection Profile templates.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: profiles saved from the Global menu are now stored as FortiWeb profiles and reach the wizard; profiles saved earlier under the Global ADOM are moved to FortiWeb at startup, unless FortiWeb already has a profile for that line.

How to use#

Declare a line#

  1. Open Global ADOM → Administrator → Line Profiles. The page runs in the FortiWeb ADOM (see the note above).
  2. Find the card of the line.
  3. In Segments this line receives, select one or more segments (use Ctrl or Cmd to select several).
  4. Choose the Certificate class (server, clientserver or client), or leave — not decided —.
  5. Optionally fill IPAM pool override. When it is blank, the segment's CIDR is used.
  6. Choose the Web Protection Profile template. Each option shows the name, version and status. Only an approved template can be used to build a policy.
  7. Optionally add a Note.
  8. Click Save profile. The flash reads Line profile for '<line>' created. (or updated.)

Delete a profile#

  1. On the line's card, click Delete profile (falls back to the guess).
  2. The flash reads Profile for '<line>' deleted — this line falls back to matching segments by name, which is a guess, not a declaration.

The buttons Network segments and Classification at the top of the page open the two pages a profile depends on.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Segments this line receives Network segments by name. Unknown names are refused No dmz-web
Certificate class server, clientserver or client. Blank = not decided No server
IPAM pool override Pool to allocate addresses from instead of the segment CIDR. Max. 128 characters No 192.0.2.0/26
Web Protection Profile template A web-protection-profile template of this product No wpp-baseline v3 — approved
Note Free text, max. 2,000 characters No Owned by the web team

Example#

🧪Example — Declaring the production line

The Lines catalog contains production. Two segments, dmz-web (192.0.2.0/24) and dmz-api (198.51.100.0/24), carry line=production. Without a profile, the card shows inferred — no profile and both segments. The admin opens Line Profiles, selects only dmz-web, picks certificate class server and the approved template wpp-baseline v3 — approved, and saves. The card turns declared, and the wizard now offers only dmz-web for production policies, with that template.

Result#

  • The profile is stored for (product, line). One profile per line and product.
  • The wizard uses it for every new policy on that line.
  • Renaming the line in Classification moves the profile with it. Clearing the line's references deletes the profile.
  • The Audit Log records line_profile.save (with the segment count, certificate class and template id) and line_profile.delete.

Troubleshooting#

The wizard still says "No profile for this line" after I saved one#

Possible causes - A profile saved under the Global ADOM before 2.11.0 was not moved at startup, because FortiWeb already had a profile for the same line. The wizard reads the FortiWeb profile. - The line of the wizard run is not the line you declared.

Solution 1. Open Line Profiles and check the card of the line the wizard uses. 2. Declare or correct the profile there and save.

Verification - The card shows declared, and the wizard no longer shows the inferred warning for that line.

"Unknown segment(s): "#

Possible causes - A selected segment was renamed or deleted on the Network Segments page while this page was open.

Solution 1. Reload the page and select the segments again.

Verification - The save flash reads Line profile for '<line>' created. or updated.

"'' is not in the Lines catalog."#

Possible causes - The line was renamed or removed in Classification after the page loaded.

Solution 1. Reload the page. Only current lines have cards.

Verification - The card for the line is present after reload.

"That Web Protection Profile template does not belong to this product."#

Possible causes - The submitted template is not a FortiWeb Web Protection Profile template.

Solution 1. Reload the page and choose a template from the list. The list offers only FortiWeb Web Protection Profile templates.

Verification - The save succeeds and the card shows no wpp_wrong_product problem.

The card shows blocks policy creation with wpp_not_approved#

Possible causes - The named template is pending or was rejected.

Solution 1. Have an administrator approve it in the Template Library, or pick an approved template.

Verification - The wpp_not_approved problem disappears from the card.

Advanced#

Advanced How the plan is computed
  • services/line_profiles.line_plan is the only place the answer is computed. This page and the wizard both call it.
  • A declared profile never falls back to the inferred match. A profile whose segments no longer resolve stays declared, with missing_segment problems.
  • Segments are stored by name, in order, without duplicates. The segments list is rewritten whole on every edit, so names are more stable than positions.
  • The address pool used by the wizard is the profile's IPAM pool override if set, else the chosen segment's CIDR. With neither, the wizard must ask.
#line profile#line#segment#certificate class#wpp template#ipam pool#wizard
